## TL;DR

Implemented the three UI fixes in task #1050. Active task controls now respect the server-backed handoff state, successful commits close the uncommitted changes panel, and adjacent repeated stderr output is presented as a neutral expandable diagnostic with its count and time span. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the branch head.

## Work and rationale

For E1, the board card now withholds its active-task action when a handoff is underway and the engineer process is no longer running. In the drawer, Start/Restart work is hidden when either the engineer is running or `handoffBusy` is true; request review is already gated by that same busy state. The status area and controls use the existing handoff tracking, which reflects server-side progress, including after reload. This prevents a second engineer from starting while a handoff is verifying the branch. When handoff completes, the existing active-task action returns according to whether an engineer is running.

For E2, `RepoDirtyPanel.commit()` keeps its success toast as the result summary, refreshes repository status, and closes the panel after a successful commit. Closing happens after refresh completes, regardless of whether other dirty files remain, matching the intended decision that the toast reports the committed result. Failures still follow the catch path: the panel remains open and displays the error and available hook output. The old in-panel committed note was unnecessary once success closes the panel.

For E3, the chat row transform now folds only adjacent identical stderr entries into one row. It tracks the count, first timestamp, and latest timestamp, while retaining diagnostic text for expansion. A different entry ends the run, preserving transcript order and distinctions. The diagnostic row is styled neutrally, so ordinary CLI stderr no longer looks like a turn failure; actual failed events continue to use their existing failure presentation. The transform runs at the display layer and leaves the source transcript intact. Both Dev chat render locations pass the grouping metadata to the shared row component.

Tests cover the repeated stderr grouping and its time bounds, different-line boundaries, neutral stderr rendering, commit-panel success and failure behavior, and handoff-aware action visibility. I also declared a task-drawer screenshot fixture for the running-checks state so the review capture can focus on the changed control area.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the existing card and drawer action paths, the shared handoff signal, the repository commit flow, and the normalized chat row builder. Reusing the handoff signal avoided maintaining a second status model in the UI. For stderr, grouping at the row transformation boundary keeps storage and streaming semantics unchanged while allowing a growing final run to update its count and latest time. For commits, closing only after the awaited status refresh avoids leaving a clean-tree state visible after a success toast, while the separate error branch naturally preserves the panel for diagnosis.

## Challenges and blockers

The changed-path check runs on the remote validation runner and includes a full UI build plus many test files, so completion took several minutes. The rendered contrast audit examined all configured theme and screen combinations and took about two and a half minutes; it passed. The test output included existing Vue/jsdom warnings from unrelated fixtures, but all scoped tests passed. No implementation blocker remained.

## Key learnings

The “running checks” indication and task actions need to derive from the same handoff state; agent-process liveness alone does not describe server-side verification. Closing a successful commit panel is clearer when the success toast already includes commit details, and failure visibility remains important because hook output can be actionable. Repeated streaming diagnostics can be reduced substantially without losing evidence by grouping only consecutive exact matches and preserving the original text and time bounds on expansion. The branch was not staged or committed in this session; RepoOS owns checkpointing and handoff finalization.
